newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares dip at noon in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares dip at noon in volatile trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market edged lower in volatile trade on Monday morning, dragged down by sharp declines in the A share market just ahead of the mid-session close, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.48 points or 0.32 percent to 148.67 after hitting a high of 152.50. Turnover was HK$41 million.
The A share index rose 5.71 points or 1.27 percent to 455.68, but off an intra-session high of 467.63. Turnover was a heavy eight billion yuan against 9.3 billion yuan for the full Friday session.

The A share market gains were based on expectations among investors that Beijing was unlikely to announce new anti-speculation measures in the last week ahead of Hong Kong reversion to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, brokers said.

"Escalating euphoria in the final days before the handover is fuelling speculation that the central government is unlikely to announce new measures to bring down share prices at least in the immediate future," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"But this is just short-term speculation, which is not going to provide strong support for prices," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Analysts said they foresaw volatile trading ahead.
On the B share market, Shenzhen Health Mineral Water was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.18 or 5.03 percent to HK$3.40.

Shenzhen's A share leader Shenzhen Development Bank was the most actively traded counter on volume of 28 million shares, rising 2.64 yuan or 7.77 percent to 36.60 yuan after hitting 10-percent limit up at 37.36 yuan.
